title: "Inter-species hourglass summary"

  path_filenames: null              # One key_data CSV path per line (filenames.txt).
  path_summary: null
  analysis_id: null
  metrics: !r c("spearman", "pearson", "Jensen-Shannon")
  comparisons: null                    # Infer actual comparison labels (e.g. Fiber-Fiber).
  species_pairs: null                  # Ordered labels: e.g. lch__vs__egr.
  condition_1: "control"
  condition_2: "control"
  permuted_side: "both"                # Both samples are randomized; checked against CSV provenance.
  shared_query_mode: "synchronized"     # synchronized | bonferroni | error (legacy parameter name).
  group_bootstrap_replicates: 3000      # Plot interval: resample observed independent sample units.
  group_bootstrap_seed: 120126
  adjust_method: "holm"
  alpha: 0.05
  bootstrap_interval_level: 0.90       # Diagnostic interval from saved bootstrap H.
  diagnostic_plots: true               # Individual effects and mean-H null histograms.
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged

# Evidence across inter-species sample pairs

Read the explicit `sample_id_1`, `sample_id_2`, `species_1`, `species_2`, and
individual IDs in the CSVs. Do not split a filename or combined `sample_id` to
recover these fields. **Keep species-pair orientation:** `lch__vs__egr` and
`egr__vs__lch` are different analyses. Preserve the comparisons actually present;
the uploaded example contains `Fiber-Fiber`, not both branches.

The uploaded analysis notebooks randomize **pseudobulk-bin order in both samples**
and evaluate similarities along each pair's **fixed observed DTW path**. Neither
sample is a fixed reference for the randomization, although sample 1 remains the
DTW query and defines the score's stages. This summary preserves that null model;
it does not establish that fixing a data-derived alignment gives a calibrated
biological no-hourglass test.

## Reused samples and the group P value

`shared_query_mode` is retained as a parameter name for existing rules, but its
checks now cover **both sides**. The default `synchronized` mode requires the new
CSV provenance: separate seeds, native-bin-input fingerprints, and actual bin
mapping hashes for each sample. Every appearance of a sample must use the same
input and transformation for the same iteration, even when its pair side changes.
Different biological individuals must use different seed schedules. A matching
seed alone is not accepted as proof of matching transformations.

`bonferroni` remains an explicit fallback for groups reusing an individual on
**either side**. It uses `min(1, number_of_pairs * min(pair_P))`; this is not a
mean-H permutation test, and has no `p_joint` or mean-H null density. `error`
rejects reuse instead. Legacy CSVs without both-side provenance can be used only
for the Bonferroni fallback (or a single-pair test); synchronized joint means
require regenerated outputs. Keep all analysis variants in separate renders.

`p_group` is the raw P value used for the report's single Holm correction across
all ordered species-pair × metric × comparison tests. For a permutation test it
is identical to `p_joint`. A group rejection is evidence against all its component
nulls being true, not proof that every pair or species has an hourglass effect.


**For mean-H tests, the statistic is unchanged:** both the observed statistic and every joint-null
statistic are arithmetic means across the same inputs. Null scores are **not**
concatenated across inputs. One row of `joint_null.csv` represents one joint
randomized configuration, not one input or one biological replicate. The null
standard deviation is not an estimate of between-plant variation.

Inference remains conditional on the specified upstream both-sample bin-order
null and any trajectories, feature sets, and stage definitions held fixed.
A numerical audit does not establish exchangeability or validate those upstream
choices. Rejection is not a claim that every sample has an effect.

Input filenames are read from `params$path_filenames` (one CSV path per line).
The Snakemake rule writes an absolute-path manifest before rendering. For interactive
Rmd debugging, provide your own manifest and set `path_filenames`, `path_summary`,
and the required analysis identifiers through `params`.

## Setup

```{r Setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = FALSE, error = FALSE)
fail <- function(...) stop(..., call. = FALSE)
text_vector <- function(x) as.character(unlist(x, use.names = FALSE))
scalar_text <- function(x) {
  is.character(x) && length(x) == 1L && !is.na(x) && nzchar(x)
}
require_columns <- function(d, required, label) {
  missing <- setdiff(required, names(d))
  if (length(missing)) fail(label, ": missing ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
constant_text <- function(d, fields, label) {
  for (nm in fields) {
    x <- as.character(d[[nm]])
    if (anyNA(x) || any(!nzchar(x)) || length(unique(x)) != 1L) {
      fail(label, ": expected one nonmissing ", nm, ".")
    }
    d[[nm]] <- x
  }
  d
}
# Preserve optional metadata instead of silently dropping it across files.
bind_fill <- function(xs) {
  fields <- Reduce(union, lapply(xs, names))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(xs, function(x) {
    for (nm in setdiff(fields, names(x))) x[[nm]] <- NA
    x[, fields, drop = FALSE]
  }))
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}
key <- function(d) paste(d$sample_id, d$metric, d$comparison, sep = "\r")

read_filename_manifest <- function(path) {
  if (!scalar_text(path) || !file.exists(path)) {
    fail("Set params$path_filenames to an existing filenames.txt manifest.")
  }
  paths <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  paths <- paths[nzchar(paths)]
  if (!length(paths)) fail("The filenames.txt manifest is empty: ", path)
  missing <- paths[!file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(missing)) {
    fail("Files listed in filenames.txt do not exist: ",
         paste(utils::head(missing, 5L), collapse = ", "))
  }
  paths <- normalizePath(paths, mustWork = TRUE)
  if (anyDuplicated(paths)) fail("Duplicate paths in filenames.txt: ", path)
  paths
}

files <- read_filename_manifest(params$path_filenames)
metrics_keep <- text_vector(params$metrics)
comparisons_keep <- text_vector(params$comparisons)
# The manifest is read directly in this notebook; no command-line parsing.
message("Loaded ", length(files), " key_data CSV files from: ",
        normalizePath(params$path_filenames, mustWork = TRUE))
if (!scalar_text(params$path_summary) || !scalar_text(params$analysis_id)) {
  fail("Set path_summary and analysis_id to nonempty strings.")
}
if (!length(metrics_keep) || anyNA(metrics_keep) || any(!nzchar(metrics_keep)) ||
    anyDuplicated(metrics_keep)) fail("Invalid metrics.")
if (anyNA(comparisons_keep) || any(!nzchar(comparisons_keep)) ||
    anyDuplicated(comparisons_keep)) fail("Invalid comparisons.")
if (!scalar_text(params$adjust_method) ||
    !params$adjust_method %in% stats::p.adjust.methods) fail("Invalid adjust_method.")
if (!is.numeric(params$alpha) || length(params$alpha) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$alpha) || params$alpha <= 0 || params$alpha >= 1) fail("Invalid alpha.")

outdir <- dirname(params$path_summary)
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
outdir <- normalizePath(outdir, mustWork = TRUE)
path_summary <- file.path(outdir, basename(params$path_summary))

read_base <- function(path, extra_fields) {
  d <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  require_columns(d, c("sample_id", "metric", "comparison", "data_type",
                       "replicate_id", "seed", "H", "n_permutation", extra_fields), path)
  if (!nrow(d) || anyNA(d$data_type) ||
      any(!d$data_type %in% c("observed", "permutation", "bootstrap"))) {
    fail(path, ": invalid data_type.")
  }
  # Failed/missing bootstrap scores do not invalidate a complete permutation run.
  d <- d[d$data_type %in% c("observed", "permutation"), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) fail(path, ": no observed/permutation rows.")
  d <- constant_text(d, c("sample_id", "metric", extra_fields), path)
  if (!d$metric[1] %in% metrics_keep) fail(path, ": unexpected metric.")
  if (anyNA(d$comparison) || any(!nzchar(d$comparison))) fail(path, ": missing comparison.")
  if (length(comparisons_keep)) d <- d[d$comparison %in% comparisons_keep, , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(d)) fail(path, ": no requested comparison.")
  if (!is.numeric(d$H) || any(!is.finite(d$H))) fail(path, ": non-finite H.")
  if (!is.numeric(d$n_permutation) || any(!is.finite(d$n_permutation)) ||
      any(d$n_permutation < 1 | d$n_permutation != floor(d$n_permutation))) {
    fail(path, ": invalid n_permutation.")
  }
  d$source_file <- path
  d$source_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(path))
  d
}

validate_components <- function(scores, ids, comparisons) {
  expected <- expand.grid(sample_id = ids, metric = metrics_keep,
                          comparison = comparisons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  observed <- scores[scores$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
  if (anyDuplicated(key(observed)) || !setequal(key(observed), key(expected)) ||
      !setequal(key(scores), key(expected))) {
    fail("Incomplete/duplicated sample-or-pair x metric x comparison grid.")
  }
  lapply(split(scores, key(scores)), function(d) {
    o <- d[d$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
    p <- d[d$data_type == "permutation", , drop = FALSE]
    label <- paste(o$sample_id, o$metric, o$comparison, sep = " / ")
    B <- unique(d$n_permutation)
    if (length(B) != 1L || B > .Machine$integer.max || nrow(p) != B) {
      fail(label, ": incomplete permutation count.")
    }
    if (anyNA(p$replicate_id) || any(!grepl("^Permutation-[1-9][0-9]*$", p$replicate_id))) {
      fail(label, ": invalid permutation IDs.")
    }
    p$iteration <- as.integer(sub("^Permutation-", "", p$replicate_id))
    if (anyNA(p$iteration) || anyDuplicated(p$iteration) ||
        !setequal(p$iteration, seq_len(B))) fail(label, ": incomplete/duplicate iteration IDs.")
    p <- p[order(p$iteration), , drop = FALSE]
    if (!is.numeric(p$seed) || any(!is.finite(p$seed)) || anyDuplicated(p$seed) ||
        any(p$seed != floor(p$seed)) || any(abs(p$seed) > .Machine$integer.max)) {
      fail(label, ": invalid/duplicate permutation seeds.")
    }
    if (all(c("Early", "Middle", "Late") %in% names(d))) {
      h <- pmin(d$Middle - d$Early, d$Middle - d$Late)
      if (any(!is.finite(h)) || any(abs(h - d$H) > 1e-8)) fail(label, ": inconsistent H.")
    }
    list(observed = o, permutation = p)
  })
}
component_summary <- function(components) {
  bind_fill(lapply(components, function(x) {
    o <- x$observed
    z <- o[, setdiff(names(o), c("data_type", "replicate_id", "seed")), drop = FALSE]
    names(z)[names(z) == "H"] <- "H_observed"
    z$n_null_ge_observed <- sum(x$permutation$H >= o$H)
    z$p_empirical <- (1 + z$n_null_ge_observed) / (1 + nrow(x$permutation))
    z
  }))
}
# Match actual transformations and native-bin inputs for EVERY reused endpoint.
hash_bin_shuffle <- function(sample_id, input_hash, bins, order) {
  digest::digest(list(version = "both_bin_order_fixed_path_v1",
                      sample_id = enc2utf8(as.character(sample_id)),
                      input_hash = as.character(input_hash),
                      target_bins = enc2utf8(as.character(bins)),
                      source_bins = enc2utf8(as.character(bins[order]))),
                 algo = "sha256", serializeVersion = 2)
}
check_both_side_sync <- function(selected) {
  records <- lapply(selected, function(x) {
    o <- x$observed; p <- x$permutation
    required_sync <- c("permutation_scheme", "permuted_sides", "permutation_unit",
                       "permutation_alignment", "permutation_rng",
                       paste0("seed_", 1:2), paste0("bin_input_hash_", 1:2),
                       paste0("shuffle_hash_", 1:2), paste0("bin_order_", 1:2),
                       paste0("permutation_bin_labels_", 1:2))
    if (!all(required_sync %in% names(p))) {
      fail(o$sample_id, ": missing both-side synchronization provenance. Regenerate its key_data CSV.")
    }
    expected <- c(permutation_scheme = "both_bin_order_fixed_path_v1",
                  permuted_sides = "1,2", permutation_unit = "pseudobulk_bin",
                  permutation_alignment = "observed_path_fixed",
                  permutation_rng = "Mersenne-Twister/Inversion/Rejection")
    for (nm in names(expected)) {
      v <- c(as.character(o[[nm]]), as.character(p[[nm]]))
      if (anyNA(v) || length(unique(v)) != 1L || v[1] != expected[[nm]]) {
        fail(o$sample_id, ": inconsistent or unsupported ", nm, ".")
      }
    }
    lapply(1:2, function(side) {
      id <- as.character(o[[paste0("sample_id_", side)]])
      unit <- paste(o[[paste0("species_", side)]], o[[paste0("individual_id_", side)]], sep = "::")
      seeds <- p[[paste0("seed_", side)]]
      input_hash <- as.character(p[[paste0("bin_input_hash_", side)]])
      hashes <- as.character(p[[paste0("shuffle_hash_", side)]])
      labels <- as.character(p[[paste0("permutation_bin_labels_", side)]])
      orders <- as.character(p[[paste0("bin_order_", side)]])
      if (!is.numeric(seeds) || any(!is.finite(seeds)) || anyDuplicated(seeds) ||
          any(seeds != floor(seeds)) || any(abs(seeds) > .Machine$integer.max)) {
        fail(id, ": invalid per-sample permutation seed vector.")
      }
      if (anyNA(input_hash) || anyNA(hashes) ||
          any(!grepl("^[0-9a-f]{64}$", input_hash)) ||
          any(!grepl("^[0-9a-f]{64}$", hashes)) ||
          length(unique(input_hash)) != 1L || anyNA(labels) ||
          length(unique(labels)) != 1L || anyNA(orders)) fail(id, ": invalid shuffle provenance.")
      if (as.character(o[[paste0("bin_input_hash_", side)]]) != input_hash[1] ||
          as.character(o[[paste0("permutation_bin_labels_", side)]]) != labels[1]) {
        fail(id, ": observed and permuted bin inputs disagree.")
      }
      bins <- strsplit(labels[1], "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      if (length(bins) < 2L || any(!nzchar(bins)) || anyDuplicated(bins)) fail(id, ": invalid bin labels.")
      for (b in seq_len(nrow(p))) {
        order <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(strsplit(orders[b], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
        if (length(order) != length(bins) || anyNA(order) ||
            !identical(sort(order), seq_along(bins))) fail(id, ": invalid stored bin permutation.")
        expected_hash <- hash_bin_shuffle(id, input_hash[b], bins, order)
        if (!identical(hashes[b], expected_hash)) fail(id, ": shuffle hash does not match the stored mapping.")
      }
      data.frame(sample_id = id, biological_unit = unit, pair_id = o$sample_id,
                 side = side, iteration = p$iteration, seed = seeds,
                 bin_input_hash = input_hash, shuffle_hash = hashes,
                 bin_order = orders, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
  })
  long <- bind_fill(unlist(records, recursive = FALSE))
  by_unit <- split(long, long$biological_unit)
  if (any(vapply(by_unit, function(z) length(unique(z$sample_id)) != 1L, logical(1)))) {
    fail("Different preparations share a biological individual. Resolve replication before joint testing.")
  }
  signature <- lapply(by_unit, function(z) {
    # Compare a sample even if it appears on different sides or in different species-pair groups.
    for (nm in c("seed", "bin_input_hash", "shuffle_hash", "bin_order")) {
      counts <- vapply(split(z[[nm]], z$iteration), function(v) length(unique(v)), integer(1))
      if (any(counts != 1L)) fail(unique(z$sample_id), ": mismatched ", nm, " across reused appearances.")
    }
    if (length(unique(z$bin_input_hash)) != 1L) fail(unique(z$sample_id), ": different native-bin inputs.")
    first <- z[z$pair_id == z$pair_id[1] & z$side == z$side[1], , drop = FALSE]
    first[order(first$iteration), , drop = FALSE]
  })
  if (length(signature) > 1L) for (i in 2:length(signature)) for (j in seq_len(i - 1L)) {
    a <- signature[[i]]; b <- signature[[j]]
    common <- intersect(a$iteration, b$iteration)
    if (length(common) && identical(as.numeric(a$seed[match(common, a$iteration)]),
                                    as.numeric(b$seed[match(common, b$iteration)]))) {
      fail(a$sample_id[1], " and ", b$sample_id[1], ": identical schedules for distinct biological samples.")
    }
  }
  bind_fill(lapply(by_unit, function(z) {
    data.frame(sample_id = z$sample_id[1], biological_unit = z$biological_unit[1],
               sides = paste(sort(unique(z$side)), collapse = ","),
               n_pair_appearances = length(unique(z$pair_id)),
               n_iterations = length(unique(z$iteration)),
               bin_input_hash = z$bin_input_hash[1], synchronization_verified = TRUE)
  }))
}
mean_test <- function(selected) {
  p <- lapply(selected, function(x) x$permutation)
  iterations <- p[[1]]$iteration
  if (!all(vapply(p, function(z) identical(z$iteration, iterations), logical(1)))) {
    fail("Different permutation ID sets within a joint test; complete the runs first.")
  }
  H <- vapply(selected, function(x) x$observed$H, numeric(1))
  T_null <- rowMeans(do.call(cbind, lapply(p, function(z) z$H)))
  T_obs <- mean(H)
  B <- length(T_null)
  k <- sum(T_null >= T_obs)
  list(H = H, iterations = iterations, null = T_null, mean_H = T_obs,
       B = B, k = k, p = (1 + k) / (B + 1))
}
# Independent arithmetic route: aggregate the original long table, not H_null.
audit_mean <- function(d, result) {
  o <- d[d$data_type == "observed", , drop = FALSE]
  p <- d[d$data_type == "permutation", , drop = FALSE]
  coverage <- table(p$replicate_id, p$sample_id)
  stopifnot(nrow(o) == length(result$H), !anyDuplicated(o$sample_id),
            setequal(o$sample_id, colnames(coverage)), all(coverage == 1L))
  reference <- aggregate(H ~ replicate_id, data = p, FUN = mean)
  reference$iteration <- as.integer(sub("^Permutation-", "", reference$replicate_id))
  reference <- reference[order(reference$iteration), , drop = FALSE]
  k <- sum(reference$H >= mean(o$H))
  delta <- max(abs(reference$H - result$null))
  stopifnot(identical(reference$iteration, result$iterations),
            length(reference$H) == result$B, k == result$k,
            abs(mean(o$H) - result$mean_H) < 1e-12, delta < 1e-12,
            abs((1 + k) / (1 + nrow(reference)) - result$p) < 1e-12)
  data.frame(audit_pass = TRUE, null_max_abs_difference = delta,
             p_recalculated = (1 + k) / (1 + nrow(reference)))
}

species_pairs_keep <- text_vector(params$species_pairs)
if (anyNA(species_pairs_keep) || any(!nzchar(species_pairs_keep)) ||

if (!scalar_text(params$condition_1) || !scalar_text(params$condition_2)) fail("Set both conditions.")
if (!identical(as.character(params$permuted_side), "both")) {
  fail("This notebook summarizes both-sample randomizations: set permuted_side = 'both'.")
}
if (!requireNamespace("digest", quietly = TRUE)) fail("Install the digest package.")
if (!is.numeric(params$group_bootstrap_replicates) || length(params$group_bootstrap_replicates) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$group_bootstrap_replicates) || params$group_bootstrap_replicates < 2 ||
    params$group_bootstrap_replicates != floor(params$group_bootstrap_replicates) ||
    params$group_bootstrap_replicates > .Machine$integer.max) fail("Invalid group_bootstrap_replicates.")
if (!is.numeric(params$group_bootstrap_seed) || length(params$group_bootstrap_seed) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$group_bootstrap_seed) ||
    params$group_bootstrap_seed != floor(params$group_bootstrap_seed) ||
    abs(params$group_bootstrap_seed) > .Machine$integer.max) fail("Invalid group_bootstrap_seed.")
if (!scalar_text(params$shared_query_mode) ||
    !params$shared_query_mode %in% c("bonferroni", "error", "synchronized")) {
  fail("Invalid shared_query_mode.")
}
sidecars <- file.path(outdir, c("pair_summary.csv", "joint_null.csv", "audit.csv",
                                "synchronization_audit.csv"))
if (path_summary %in% c(files, sidecars) || any(sidecars %in% files)) fail("Conflicting output paths.")

# Diagnostics only: none of these functions changes the observed/permuted test.
if (!is.numeric(params$bootstrap_interval_level) ||
    length(params$bootstrap_interval_level) != 1L ||
    !is.finite(params$bootstrap_interval_level) ||
    params$bootstrap_interval_level <= 0 || params$bootstrap_interval_level >= 1) {
  fail("bootstrap_interval_level must be between 0 and 1.")
}
if (!is.logical(params$diagnostic_plots) || length(params$diagnostic_plots) != 1L ||
    is.na(params$diagnostic_plots)) fail("diagnostic_plots must be TRUE or FALSE.")

# Read the saved bootstrap H values separately; NEVER put them in the null matrix.
add_component_diagnostics <- function(tab, group_columns) {
  raw <- lapply(files, function(path) {
    read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  })
  ids <- paste(tab$sample_id, tab$metric, tab$comparison, sep = "\r")
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ids))
  prob <- c((1 - params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2,
            (1 + params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2)
  diagnostics <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tab)), function(i) {
    j <- match(tab$source_file[i], files)
    if (is.na(j)) fail("Diagnostic source file is absent from the input list.")
    d <- raw[[j]]
    same <- d$sample_id == tab$sample_id[i] & d$metric == tab$metric[i] &
      d$comparison == tab$comparison[i]
    o <- d[which(same & d$data_type == "observed"), , drop = FALSE]
    b <- d[which(same & d$data_type == "bootstrap"), , drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(nrow(o) == 1L)
    if (nrow(b) && (anyNA(b$replicate_id) || any(!nzchar(b$replicate_id)) ||
                   anyDuplicated(b$replicate_id))) {
      fail(tab$sample_id[i], ": missing/duplicate bootstrap IDs.")
    }
    if (nrow(b) && !is.numeric(b$H)) fail("Non-numeric saved bootstrap H values.")
    h <- b$H[is.finite(b$H)]
    interval <- if (length(h) >= 2L) {
      unname(stats::quantile(h, probs = prob, type = 7))
    } else c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
    reported <- function(name) {
      if (!name %in% names(o)) return(NA_real_)
      value <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(o[[name]]))
      if (length(value) != 1L || !is.finite(value)) return(NA_real_)
      value
    }
    valid_reported <- reported("n_bootstrap_valid")
    metadata_ok <- if (is.na(valid_reported)) NA else valid_reported == length(h)
    data.frame(
      bootstrap_n_saved = nrow(b), bootstrap_n_finite = length(h),
      bootstrap_n_nonfinite = nrow(b) - length(h),
      bootstrap_n_requested_reported = reported("n_bootstrap_requested"),
      bootstrap_n_valid_reported = valid_reported,
      bootstrap_n_failed_reported = reported("n_bootstrap_failed"),
      bootstrap_metadata_ok = metadata_ok,
      bootstrap_status = if (!nrow(b)) "not_available" else if (length(h) < 2L) {
        "too_few_finite_draws"
      } else if (isFALSE(metadata_ok)) "metadata_mismatch" else "available",
      bootstrap_interval_level = params$bootstrap_interval_level,
      H_bootstrap_median = if (length(h)) stats::median(h) else NA_real_,
      H_bootstrap_lower = interval[1], H_bootstrap_upper = interval[2],
      uncertainty_scope = "within_input_resampling_not_between_individuals",
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
  tab <- cbind(tab, do.call(rbind, diagnostics))
  if (any(tab$bootstrap_status == "metadata_mismatch")) {
    warning("Saved bootstrap counts differ from declared n_bootstrap_valid; inspect component diagnostics.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Both endpoints are randomized. Omit all incident pairs for each endpoint separately.
  tab$mean_H_without_individual_1 <- NA_real_
  tab$mean_H_without_individual_2 <- NA_real_
  groups <- do.call(paste, c(tab[group_columns], sep = "\r"))
  for (index in split(seq_len(nrow(tab)), groups)) for (i in index) for (side in 1:2) {
    unit <- tab[[paste0("individual_key_", side)]][i]
    retained <- index[tab$individual_key_1[index] != unit & tab$individual_key_2[index] != unit]
    if (length(retained)) tab[[paste0("mean_H_without_individual_", side)]][i] <- mean(tab$H_observed[retained])
  }
  tab
}

# Separate plots for each test; intervals are within-input bootstrap percentiles,
# not a confidence interval for the species-wide or population-average effect.
plot_component_effects <- function(tab, group_columns, label_columns) {
  old <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old), add = TRUE)
  groups <- do.call(paste, c(tab[group_columns], sep = " | "))
  for (label in unique(groups)) {
    d <- tab[groups == label, , drop = FALSE]
    labels <- do.call(paste, c(d[label_columns], sep = " vs "))
    y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(d)))
    xr <- range(c(0, d$H_observed, d$H_bootstrap_lower, d$H_bootstrap_upper),
                finite = TRUE)
    padding <- max(diff(xr) * 0.08, 0.01)
    graphics::par(mar = c(4.2, 15, 3.5, 1))
    graphics::plot(d$H_observed, y, xlim = xr + c(-padding, padding),
                   ylim = c(0.5, nrow(d) + 0.5), pch = 19, yaxt = "n",
                   ylab = "", xlab = "Observed hourglass score H", main = label)
    graphics::axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
    valid <- is.finite(d$H_bootstrap_lower) & is.finite(d$H_bootstrap_upper)
    graphics::segments(d$H_bootstrap_lower[valid], y[valid],
                       d$H_bootstrap_upper[valid], y[valid])
    graphics::abline(v = 0, lty = 3)
    graphics::mtext(sprintf("Bars: %.0f%% within-input bootstrap percentile intervals; no bar when unavailable",
                            100 * params$bootstrap_interval_level),
                    side = 1, line = 3, cex = 0.7)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
plot_mean_nulls <- function(summary, null, group_columns) {
  old <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(graphics::par(old), add = TRUE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary))) {
    s <- summary[i, , drop = FALSE]
    keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(null))
    for (nm in group_columns) keep <- keep & null[[nm]] == s[[nm]]
    x <- null$mean_H_null[keep]
    label <- paste(unlist(s[group_columns], use.names = FALSE), collapse = " | ")
    if (!length(x)) {
      message(label, ": no mean-H null; inspect p_method and p_group.")
      next
    }
    graphics::par(mar = c(4.5, 4.2, 4, 1))
    graphics::hist(x, breaks = "FD", xlim = range(c(x, s$mean_H)),
                   main = label, xlab = "Mean H across inputs in ONE joint permutation",
                   ylab = "Joint permutations")
    graphics::abline(v = s$mean_H, lwd = 2)
    graphics::mtext(sprintf("Observed mean H = %.4f; B = %d; exceedances = %d; P = %.4g; adjusted P = %.4g",
                            s$mean_H, s$n_joint_permutation, s$n_null_ge_observed,
                            s$p_joint, s$p_adjusted), side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 0.7)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

params
```

## Read and validate the key data

```{r Read key data}
metadata_fields <- c("sample_id_1", "sample_id_2", "species_1", "species_2",
                     "individual_id_1", "individual_id_2", "condition_1", "condition_2")
inputs <- lapply(files, function(path) {
  d <- read_base(path, metadata_fields)
  if (d$species_1[1] == d$species_2[1]) fail(path, ": not an inter-species pair.")
  if (d$condition_1[1] != params$condition_1 || d$condition_2[1] != params$condition_2) {
    fail(path, ": unexpected condition_1/condition_2.")
  }
  d$species_pair <- paste(d$species_1, d$species_2, sep = "__vs__")
  if (length(species_pairs_keep) && !d$species_pair[1] %in% species_pairs_keep) {
    fail(path, ": unexpected ordered species_pair.")
  }
  d$individual_key_1 <- paste(d$species_1, d$individual_id_1, sep = "::")
  d$individual_key_2 <- paste(d$species_2, d$individual_id_2, sep = "::")
  d
})
scores <- bind_fill(inputs)
if (!length(species_pairs_keep)) species_pairs_keep <- unique(scores$species_pair)
if (!setequal(unique(scores$species_pair), species_pairs_keep)) fail("A requested species_pair is missing.")
if (!length(comparisons_keep)) comparisons_keep <- sort(unique(scores$comparison))
manifest_fields <- c("sample_id", metadata_fields, "species_pair", "individual_key_1", "individual_key_2")
manifest <- unique(scores[c("source_file", "metric", manifest_fields)])
if (anyDuplicated(manifest[c("sample_id", "metric")])) fail("Duplicate pair/metric input files.")
pair_metadata <- unique(manifest[manifest_fields])
if (anyDuplicated(pair_metadata$sample_id) ||
    anyDuplicated(pair_metadata[c("sample_id_1", "sample_id_2")])) {
  fail("Inconsistent pair metadata or multiple IDs for the same ordered sample pair.")
}
# A sample must keep its biological-individual/species identity across all pairings.
all_samples <- unique(rbind(
  data.frame(sample = pair_metadata$sample_id_1, species = pair_metadata$species_1,
             individual = pair_metadata$individual_id_1),
  data.frame(sample = pair_metadata$sample_id_2, species = pair_metadata$species_2,
             individual = pair_metadata$individual_id_2)
))
if (anyDuplicated(all_samples$sample)) fail("Inconsistent biological metadata for a reused sample.")
components <- validate_components(scores, pair_metadata$sample_id, comparisons_keep)
pair_summary <- component_summary(components)
pair_summary$analysis_id <- params$analysis_id
pair_summary <- add_component_diagnostics(pair_summary, c("species_pair", "metric", "comparison"))
# In strict mode, audit shared samples across ALL species-pair groups in this render.
synchronization_audit <- data.frame(
  metric = character(), comparison = character(), sample_id = character(),
  biological_unit = character(), sides = character(), n_pair_appearances = integer(),
  n_iterations = integer(), bin_input_hash = character(), synchronization_verified = logical()
)
if (params$shared_query_mode == "synchronized") {
  checks <- expand.grid(metric = metrics_keep, comparison = comparisons_keep, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  synchronization_audit <- bind_fill(lapply(seq_len(nrow(checks)), function(i) {
    lookup <- data.frame(sample_id = pair_metadata$sample_id,
                         metric = checks$metric[i], comparison = checks$comparison[i])
    cbind(checks[i, , drop = FALSE], check_both_side_sync(components[key(lookup)]))
  }))
}
pair_metadata[c("sample_id_1", "sample_id_2", "species_pair", "individual_key_1", "individual_key_2")]
```

## Group tests with dependence checks

The mean-H statistic gives each input pair equal weight. It is not an average
across independent plants when pairs reuse plants. Independent source samples,
valid within-pair randomizations, and unchanged observed/permutation feature
selection remain assumptions. Bootstrap rows are never used as null draws.

```{r Group tests}
tests <- expand.grid(species_pair = species_pairs_keep, metric = metrics_keep,
                     comparison = comparisons_keep, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tests)), function(i) {
  test <- tests[i, , drop = FALSE]
  pm <- pair_metadata[pair_metadata$species_pair == test$species_pair, , drop = FALSE]
  ids <- pm$sample_id
  selected <- components[key(data.frame(sample_id = ids, metric = test$metric,
                                        comparison = test$comparison))]
  p <- lapply(selected, function(x) x$permutation)
  H <- vapply(selected, function(x) x$observed$H, numeric(1))
  pair_p <- vapply(selected, function(x) {
    (1 + sum(x$permutation$H >= x$observed$H)) / (1 + nrow(x$permutation))
  }, numeric(1))
  # Avoid averaging scores based on different stage definitions or bin counts.
  for (nm in intersect(c("n_bins", "middle_cell_types", "middle_fraction", "focal_species"), names(scores))) {
    values <- unlist(lapply(selected, function(x) x$observed[[nm]]), use.names = FALSE)
    if (anyNA(values) || length(unique(values)) != 1L) fail(test$species_pair, ": mixed ", nm, ".")
  }
  all_units <- c(pm$individual_key_1, pm$individual_key_2)
  reused_any <- anyDuplicated(all_units) > 0L
  fallback <- reused_any && params$shared_query_mode == "bonferroni"
  if (reused_any && params$shared_query_mode == "error") {
    fail(test$species_pair, ": a randomized individual is reused on side 1 or side 2.")
  }
  meta <- data.frame(analysis_id = params$analysis_id, test,
                     species_1 = pm$species_1[1], species_2 = pm$species_2[1],
                     condition_1 = params$condition_1, condition_2 = params$condition_2,
                     permuted_side = params$permuted_side)
  summary <- cbind(meta, data.frame(
    n_pairs = length(ids), pairs = paste(ids, collapse = ";"),
    n_individuals_1 = length(unique(pm$individual_id_1)),
    n_individuals_2 = length(unique(pm$individual_id_2)),
    n_randomized_individuals = length(unique(all_units)),
    n_fixed_individuals = 0L,
    reused_randomized_individual = reused_any,
    reused_individual_1 = anyDuplicated(pm$individual_key_1) > 0L,
    reused_individual_2 = anyDuplicated(pm$individual_key_2) > 0L,
    n_randomization_units = length(unique(all_units)),
    synchronization_verified = FALSE,
    mean_H = mean(H), median_H = median(H), min_H = min(H), max_H = max(H),
    sd_H = if (length(H) > 1L) sd(H) else NA_real_,
    n_positive_H = sum(H > 0), fraction_positive_H = mean(H > 0)
  ))
  d <- scores[scores$species_pair == test$species_pair & scores$metric == test$metric &
                scores$comparison == test$comparison, , drop = FALSE]
  # Empty but typed output is intentional when no mean-H joint null is valid.
  null <- cbind(meta[FALSE, , drop = FALSE],
                data.frame(iteration = integer(), mean_H_null = numeric()))
  if (fallback) {
    summary$p_method <- "bonferroni_min_pair_p"
    summary$test_scope <- "global_pair_null_not_mean_H"
    summary$p_group <- min(1, length(pair_p) * min(pair_p))
    summary$p_joint <- NA_real_
    summary$n_joint_permutation <- NA_integer_
    summary$n_null_ge_observed <- NA_integer_
    summary$p_resolution <- NA_real_
    summary$at_minimum_resolution <- NA
    summary$null_mean_H <- summary$null_sd_H <- NA_real_
    summary$null_min_H <- summary$null_max_H <- NA_real_
    summary$observed_minus_null_mean <- NA_real_
    best <- which.min(pair_p)
    summary$best_pair <- ids[best]
    summary$best_pair_p <- pair_p[best]
    summary$best_pair_H <- H[best]
    # Recompute every component P directly from the long table for the audit.
    parts <- split(d, d$sample_id)
    check_p <- vapply(parts, function(z) {
      obs <- z$H[z$data_type == "observed"]
      nul <- z$H[z$data_type == "permutation"]
      stopifnot(length(obs) == 1L)
      (1 + sum(nul >= obs)) / (1 + length(nul))
    }, numeric(1))
    p_check <- min(1, length(parts) * min(check_p))
    stopifnot(abs(mean(d$H[d$data_type == "observed"]) - summary$mean_H) < 1e-12,
              abs(p_check - summary$p_group) < 1e-12)
    audit <- cbind(meta, data.frame(audit_pass = TRUE, null_max_abs_difference = NA_real_,
                                   p_recalculated = p_check))
  } else {
    # New joint tests require both endpoint schedules and matching mapping hashes.
    # A legacy single-pair P can be read without establishing cross-pair synchronization.
    if (length(ids) > 1L || params$shared_query_mode == "synchronized") {
      check_both_side_sync(selected)
      summary$synchronization_verified <- TRUE
    }
    r <- mean_test(selected)
    summary$p_method <- if (length(ids) == 1L) "single_pair_permutation" else {
      "synchronized_both_samples_mean_permutation"
    }
    summary$test_scope <- if (length(ids) == 1L) "single_pair" else "both_samples_joint_pairs"
    summary$p_group <- summary$p_joint <- r$p
    summary$n_joint_permutation <- r$B
    summary$n_null_ge_observed <- r$k
    summary$p_resolution <- 1 / (r$B + 1)
    summary$at_minimum_resolution <- r$k == 0L
    summary$null_mean_H <- mean(r$null)
    summary$null_sd_H <- sd(r$null)
    summary$null_min_H <- min(r$null)
    summary$null_max_H <- max(r$null)
    summary$observed_minus_null_mean <- r$mean_H - mean(r$null)
    summary$best_pair <- ids[which.min(pair_p)]
    summary$best_pair_p <- min(pair_p)
    summary$best_pair_H <- H[which.min(pair_p)]
    null <- cbind(meta[rep(1L, r$B), , drop = FALSE],
                  data.frame(iteration = r$iterations, mean_H_null = r$null))
    audit <- cbind(meta, audit_mean(d, r))
  }
  audit$synchronization_verified <- summary$synchronization_verified
  list(summary = summary, null = null, audit = audit)
})
summary_results <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$summary))
joint_null <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$null))
audit <- bind_fill(lapply(results, function(x) x$audit))
```

## Multiple-testing correction and export

Correct `p_group` once across **all ordered species-pair × metric × comparison**
rows in this render. For three ordered species pairs, three metrics and one
comparison, there are nine tests; with two comparisons, eighteen. The within-group
Bonferroni combination, where needed, and the across-group Holm correction address
different hypothesis levels. Do not include already adjusted pair P values.

```{r Adjust and save}
summary_results$p_adjusted <- p.adjust(summary_results$p_group, method = params$adjust_method)
summary_results$adjust_method <- params$adjust_method
summary_results$n_tests_in_family <- nrow(summary_results)
summary_results$alpha <- params$alpha
summary_results$reject_group_null <- summary_results$p_adjusted <= params$alpha
summary_results$hourglass_supported <- summary_results$reject_group_null & summary_results$mean_H > 0 &
  (summary_results$p_method != "bonferroni_min_pair_p" | summary_results$best_pair_H > 0)
audit$p_adjusted_recalculated <- p.adjust(audit$p_recalculated, method = params$adjust_method)
stopifnot(all(abs(audit$p_adjusted_recalculated - summary_results$p_adjusted) < 1e-12))
write.csv(summary_results, path_summary, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(pair_summary, sidecars[1], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(joint_null, sidecars[2], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
write.csv(audit, sidecars[3], row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
# Overwrite even in fallback mode, so an old synchronization audit cannot linger.
write.csv(synchronization_audit, sidecars[4], row.names = FALSE)
summary_results[c("species_pair", "metric", "comparison", "n_pairs", "n_individuals_1",
                  "n_individuals_2", "mean_H", "p_method", "n_joint_permutation",
                  "n_null_ge_observed", "p_resolution", "p_joint", "p_group",
                  "p_adjusted", "synchronization_verified", "hourglass_supported")]
```

`hourglass_supported` is an operational flag, not evidence of universal effects.
For the fallback it additionally requires positive H in the pair supplying the
minimum P. Always report `p_method`: **a Bonferroni global-pair test is not a
mean-H permutation test**. A single Lch preparation compared with
several Egr samples remains one Lch preparation, even though both sides are shuffled.

The summary does not estimate population-average effects. Stage definitions,
actual shuffle synchronization, pair-specific gene selection, and biological
replicate independence must be checked in the upstream analyses.


## Individual effects and uncertainty

Dots show **observed H**. Bars use the central `bootstrap_interval_level`
percentile interval of the **saved, finite bootstrap H values for that input**
(default 90%; type-7 quantiles). Missing bootstrap draws are reported, not replaced.
These are within-input resampling intervals, **not between-plant uncertainty**,
not species-pair confidence intervals, and not evidence that spatial dependence
was handled upstream. Bootstrap intervals do not determine any permutation P value.
`bootstrap_n_*` columns distinguish saved, finite, and declared counts. Intervals
are conditional on usable draws; missing H values or failed resamples can affect
their interpretation. They do not by themselves establish nominal coverage.

`mean_H_without_individual_1` and `mean_H_without_individual_2` are descriptive
leave-one-individual-out means. Each omits all pairs incident to that endpoint,
including appearances on the opposite side. With only one Lch individual, removing
it leaves no pairs, so that value is `NA`. Neither endpoint is treated as fixed
for the permutation test. Bootstrap uncertainty and permutation synchronization
are separate: matching bin shuffles does not synchronize cell bootstrap draws.

```{r Pair summary}
pair_summary[c("sample_id_1", "sample_id_2", "metric", "comparison", "H_observed",
               "H_bootstrap_lower", "H_bootstrap_upper", "bootstrap_n_finite",
               "bootstrap_status", "mean_H_without_individual_1", "mean_H_without_individual_2", "p_empirical")]
```

```{r Pair effect plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
if (params$diagnostic_plots) {
  plot_component_effects(pair_summary, c("species_pair", "metric", "comparison"),
                         c("sample_id_1", "sample_id_2"))
}
```

## Joint-null distributions

Only groups with a valid mean-H permutation test have a histogram. For a
Bonferroni fallback, `p_joint` and the mean-H null remain absent; its group P value
is in `p_group`. No pooled-null approximation is substituted.

```{r Joint null plots, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
if (params$diagnostic_plots) {
  plot_mean_nulls(summary_results, joint_null, c("species_pair", "metric", "comparison"))
}
```

## Numerical audit

```{r Numerical audit}
audit
synchronization_audit
```

The audit independently reconstructs null means and P values, or reconstructs
the Bonferroni combination directly from the component rows. Zero exceedances
are shown as the resolution floor `1 / (B + 1)`. No new permutations are generated.

## Species-pair × metric: aligned publication plots

Each figure has **one row per ordered species pair × metric** (not one row per
sample pair). Within each lineage comparison, rows are ordered by the reference
species (Ptr → Egr → Lch) and then Jensen–Shannon → Pearson → Spearman.

**When a valid joint mean-H null exists** (`p_method` indicates a joint
permutation test), the turquoise ridges show its saved per-iteration means, the
red ticks denote the observed mean H, and the text gives the one-sided group P
value and Holm adjustment. For reused randomized samples using
`shared_query_mode: bonferroni`, **there is no mean-H joint permutation null**;
these rows instead show a labelled blank baseline with the observed *descriptive*
mean and the **Bonferroni-combined `p_group`**. We do not pool pair-level null
scores, invent a ridge, or label this P value as `p_joint`.

The right-hand panel shows **observed mean H**. For a one-to-many design (e.g.
one Lch and several independent Ptr samples), grey round-ended bars bootstrap
the observed pair scores across the independent samples on the replicated side.
They are approximate intervals **conditional on the one observed sample on the
other side**; they do not incorporate that sample's cell-bootstrap uncertainty or
estimate variation among Lch individuals. For disjoint pairs, observed pair scores
are resampled as units. With a single pair, use its saved within-pair interval.
For more complicated shared-endpoint designs, omit the group bar until a suitable
joint bootstrap is available. Small numbers of biological samples limit interval
reliability. No independently generated pairwise cell bootstraps are averaged
into a purported synchronized group CI, and no CI affects a permutation P value.

```{r Inter pair metric publication plots, fig.width=15, fig.height=7.2, dpi=160, results='asis'}
if (isTRUE(params$diagnostic_plots)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) ||
      !requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) {
    warning("Install ggplot2 and patchwork to draw the inter-species publication plots.",
            call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    metric_order <- c("Jensen-Shannon", "pearson", "spearman")
    species_order <- c("ptr", "egr", "lch", "tar")
    species_label <- c("ptr" = "Ptr", "egr" = "Egr", "lch" = "Lch", "tar" = "Tar")
    ridge_colors <- c("ptr" = "#A1CFD1", "egr" = "#69A5B8",
                      "lch" = "#356E86", "tar" = "#8178A9")
    metric_label <- c("Jensen-Shannon" = "Jensen–Shannon",
                      "pearson" = "Pearson", "spearman" = "Spearman")
    metric_colors <- c("Jensen-Shannon" = "#2B9E92",
                       "pearson" = "#D77965", "spearman" = "#7C7EB8")

    set.seed(as.integer(params$group_bootstrap_seed))
    n_plot_boot <- as.integer(params$group_bootstrap_replicates)
    group_ci <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(summary_results)), function(j) {
      s <- summary_results[j, , drop = FALSE]
      z <- pair_summary[pair_summary$species_pair == s$species_pair &
                          pair_summary$metric == s$metric &
                          pair_summary$comparison == s$comparison, , drop = FALSE]
      stopifnot(nrow(z) == s$n_pairs, abs(mean(z$H_observed) - s$mean_H) < 1e-10)
      n1 <- length(unique(z$individual_key_1))
      n2 <- length(unique(z$individual_key_2))
      m <- nrow(z)
      lo <- hi <- NA_real_
      status <- "requires_dependence_aware_joint_bootstrap"
      if (m == 1L) {
        lo <- z$H_bootstrap_lower; hi <- z$H_bootstrap_upper
        status <- if (is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi)) "single_pair_within_sample_only" else "no_interval"
      } else if ((n1 == 1L && n2 == m) || (n2 == 1L && n1 == m) || (n1 == m && n2 == m)) {
        combined <- replicate(n_plot_boot, mean(z$H_observed[sample.int(m, m, replace = TRUE)]))
        ci <- unname(stats::quantile(combined,
          probs = c((1 - params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2,
                    (1 + params$bootstrap_interval_level) / 2), type = 7))
        lo <- ci[1]; hi <- ci[2]
        status <- if (n1 == 1L) "sample2_bootstrap_conditional_on_single_sample1" else if (n2 == 1L) {
          "sample1_bootstrap_conditional_on_single_sample2"
        } else "independent_pair_bootstrap"
      }
      data.frame(species_pair = as.character(s$species_pair), metric = as.character(s$metric),
                 comparison = as.character(s$comparison), ci_lower = lo, ci_upper = hi,
                 ci_scope = status, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))

    plot_summary <- merge(summary_results, group_ci,
                          by = c("species_pair", "metric", "comparison"),
                          sort = FALSE, all.x = TRUE)
    stopifnot(nrow(plot_summary) == nrow(summary_results))
    utils::write.csv(plot_summary,
                     file.path(outdir, "inter_pair_metric_effects.csv"),
                     row.names = FALSE)

    for (cmp in unique(plot_summary$comparison)) {
      s <- plot_summary[plot_summary$comparison == cmp, , drop = FALSE]
      s <- s[order(match(s$species_2, species_order),
                   match(s$species_1, species_order),
                   match(s$metric, metric_order)), , drop = FALSE]
      s$y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(s)))
      from <- unname(species_label[s$species_1])
      to <- unname(species_label[s$species_2])
      from[is.na(from)] <- s$species_1[is.na(from)]
      to[is.na(to)] <- s$species_2[is.na(to)]
      s$label <- sprintf("%s → %s · %s  (pairs=%d; n=%d/%d)",
                         from, to, metric_label[s$metric], s$n_pairs,
                         s$n_individuals_1, s$n_individuals_2)
      s$p_annotation <- sprintf("Pgroup = %.3g",
                                s$p_group)
      s$has_joint_null <- !is.na(s$p_joint)
      n <- joint_null[joint_null$comparison == cmp, , drop = FALSE]
      xr <- range(c(n$mean_H_null, s$mean_H), finite = TRUE)
      if (!is.finite(diff(xr)) || diff(xr) <= 0) xr <- xr + c(-0.01, 0.01)
      pad <- max(0.07 * diff(xr), 0.008)
      ridge <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(s)), function(i) {
        if (!s$has_joint_null[i]) return(NULL)
        v <- n$mean_H_null[n$species_pair == s$species_pair[i] &
                             n$metric == s$metric[i]]
        v <- v[is.finite(v)]
        if (length(v) < 2L || length(unique(v)) < 2L) return(NULL)
        de <- stats::density(v, from = xr[1] - pad, to = xr[2] + pad,
                             n = 256L, na.rm = TRUE)
        data.frame(x = de$x, ymin = s$y[i],
                   ymax = s$y[i] + 0.72 * de$y / max(de$y),
                   species_2 = s$species_2[i],
                   id = paste(s$species_pair[i], s$metric[i], sep = "::"),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }))
      p_perm <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
        ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = s$y, colour = "#DEE7EC", linewidth = 0.4)
      if (!is.null(ridge) && nrow(ridge)) {
        p_perm <- p_perm + ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
          data = ridge,
          ggplot2::aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax,
                       group = id, fill = species_2), alpha = 0.96) +
          ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = ridge_colors, guide = "none")
      }
      fallback_s <- s[!s$has_joint_null, , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(fallback_s)) {
        p_perm <- p_perm + ggplot2::geom_text(
          data = fallback_s,
          ggplot2::aes(x = xr[1], y = y + 0.24,
                       label = "No joint null (Bonferroni)"),
          hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "#66727C")
      }
      p_perm <- p_perm +
        ggplot2::geom_segment(
          data = s, ggplot2::aes(x = mean_H, xend = mean_H,
                                 y = y - 0.06, yend = y + 0.79),
          colour = "#BD4B41", linewidth = 0.85) +
        ggplot2::geom_text(
          data = s, ggplot2::aes(x = xr[2] + 2.7 * pad, y = y + 0.25,
                                 label = p_annotation),
          hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "#394654") +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = s$y, labels = s$label,
          limits = c(0.65, nrow(s) + 1.15), expand = c(0, 0)) +
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.025, 0.48))) +
        ggplot2::coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
        ggplot2::labs(title = "Permutation distributions / group tests",
          subtitle = "Vertical ticks: observed mean H; blank rows: Bonferroni combination",
          x = "Mean H under both-sample bin shuffling (when available)", y = NULL) +
        ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
        ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, colour = "#243447"),
          axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
          plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
          plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(5, 15, 5, 5))

      p_ci <- ggplot2::ggplot(s, ggplot2::aes(y = y)) +
        ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                            colour = "#C5CCD2", linewidth = 0.5) +
        ggplot2::geom_segment(
          data = s[is.finite(s$ci_lower) & is.finite(s$ci_upper), , drop = FALSE],
          ggplot2::aes(x = ci_lower, xend = ci_upper, yend = y),
          linewidth = 3.7, lineend = "round", colour = "#C6C9CE") +
        ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = mean_H, colour = metric), size = 3.4) +
        ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = metric_colors, guide = "none") +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = s$y, labels = rep("", nrow(s)),
          limits = c(0.65, nrow(s) + 1.15), expand = c(0, 0)) +
        ggplot2::labs(title = "Observed means & bootstrap intervals",
          subtitle = sprintf("Grey: %.0f%% interval; target depends on replication (see text)",
                             100 * params$bootstrap_interval_level),
          x = "Observed mean hourglass score H", y = NULL) +
        ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
        ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
          plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
          plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(5, 5, 5, 5))
      combined_plot <- p_perm + p_ci + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.9, 1))
      cat("\n\n### ", cmp, "\n\n", sep = "")
      print(combined_plot)
      stem <- paste0("inter_pair_metric_", gsub("[^[:alnum:]_-]", "_", cmp))
      ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(outdir, paste0(stem, ".png")),
        plot = combined_plot, width = 10, height = 5.2,
        units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
      ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(outdir, paste0(stem, ".pdf")),
        plot = combined_plot, width = 10, height = 5.2,
        units = "in", bg = "white")
      svg(
        file.path(outdir, paste0(stem, ".svg")),
        width = 10, 
        height = 5.2
      )
      print(combined_plot)
      dev.off()
      cat("\n\nInterval scope: ", paste(unique(s$ci_scope), collapse = "; "),
          ". Conditional intervals do not add biological replication to the single-sample side.\n\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
}
```
